absent: Numeric values, bit widths, and layout positions for poison fills, guard markers, cache flags, page flag masks, migration ids, free control bits, and taint codes.
Buddy merging, zone list draining, and per cpu cache capacity, batching, and draining behavior beyond the trylock commit fallback shown.
Slab creation, object initialization, freelist construction, allocation and free fast paths, and tracking record capture.
Conversions among slab, page, folio, frame number, and virtual address, including compound order and head linkage establishment.
Sanitizer metadata sizing, tag handling, poisoning integration, stack depot lifecycle, and object extension sizing and placement.
Memory cgroup charging path, online state transitions, and owner lifecycle beyond uncharge.
Lock ordering, interrupt context, and sleeping rules beyond per cpu pinning and trylock discipline.
Boot time initialization, phase transitions, and configuration selection for alternate no-op and hardened variants.

findings.text: Provides a frozen-page release entry that accepts a page and block order and forwards to the internal frozen free path with default flags.
Provides an allocation history reporting entry that emits allocation and free track records for a cache object when user tracking is enabled, otherwise does nothing.
Provides a kernel memory uncharge entry that releases the charge for a page range, clears the page association, and drops the owner reference when an owner exists.
Callable entry for returning frozen pages to the allocator; callers supply the head page and order and the implementation handles per cpu caching versus direct buddy return.
Callable entry for kernel memory uncharge during page release; invoked when online accounting indicates a charged kernel page.

Per cpu page cache access pins the current task, obtains the per cpu structure for the zone set, and attempts a nonblocking lock; failure unpins and yields no structure, success requires an unlock that releases the spin lock then unpins. An alternate configuration never provides a structure and treats unlock as fatal misuse. Frozen free uses trylock success for cached commit and falls back to direct buddy return when locking fails, and queues to a zone list when nolock context cannot spin.

Frozen release first rejects orders outside the cacheable set to direct buddy return, then runs preparation which can veto further handling. It resolves the block migration class, diverts isolated blocks to direct return, normalizes high atomic and contiguous classes to movable, and then either enqueues without locking, commits to the per cpu cache under trylock, or returns directly when the cache is unavailable.

Cacheable orders include all orders up to the costly threshold and additionally include the huge page middle directory order when transparent huge page support is present; larger orders bypass the per cpu cache.

Pageblock metadata is addressed through a bitmap whose base comes from the sparse section usemap or from zone flags. The bit index derives from a section or zone relative frame number shifted by block order and scaled by bits per block, then split into a word pointer and an intra word offset. Width, type range, and zone span are validated with compile time and debug checks.

Migration class extraction reads one bitmap word once and applies a mask covering type plus isolate, reports isolate as a distinct class when isolation support marks it, and otherwise returns the low type bits. The single read keeps racy concurrent updates from producing torn values.

Preparation starts with a prepared short circuit and a tail assertion, then handles deferred reclamation ownership by clearing the marker, counting the event, deferring the folio, and vetoing immediate return, with a warning if nolock context is used and an exception for poisoned order zero pages.

Charged kernel pages are uncharged only when accounting is online and the page carries the marker. A lingering lockable marker is cleared with per zone and event accounting. Poisoned order zero pages are diverted from caches and buddy handling after owner, table check, and tag cleanup plus tag reference clearing.

Compound preparation asserts that compound order matches the free order, clears second page flags and large folio counts when compound, then iterates over tail pages to run compound tail preparation and optional bad state and private checks, clearing tail validation flags on each tail.

Finalization detaches anonymous mappings with huge page statistics, resets overlayed page type, aborts on optional bad state detection, resets identity, clears validation flags and private data, runs owner table and tag cleanup, performs lock and object debug checks for low memory lockable frees, orders kernel and sanitizer poisoning with initialization, then invokes the architecture hook and debug unmap before reporting success.

Kernel memory ownership is decoded from a tagged association word where disabled accounting or zero means no owner, the low flag pattern must indicate kernel memory, and the owner pointer is recovered by removing the tag. Uncharge releases the page count, clears the association word, and drops the owner reference.

Bad page reporting allows a burst of sixty messages then quiets for a minute while counting suppressed reports, emits an alert with process name and frame number plus page, module, and stack dumps, clears the buddy marker to avoid allocator trouble, and taints the kernel as unreliable.

Expected free state requires a negative one map count, null mapping, zero reference count, zero cgroup association, no pool ownership, and no checked flags. A reason selector maps each violated condition to a diagnostic label and distinguishes preparation flag violations from free time flag violations; the predicate reports bad state after emitting the report.

Tail validation depends on position within the block: the first tail checks large and per page mapping counts and width dependent whole mapping and pin counts, the second checks deferred list emptiness with width dependent placement of the whole and pin checks, later tails require a tail marker except for huge table pages, all tails require the tail marker flag and consistent head linkage, then clear the marker and head link; disabled checking skips validation and reports success.

Slab objects are laid out with an optional left guard before the logical base, a user visible body, a right guard or alignment filler up to the used length, and a trailer after the information end holding user tracks, original size, sanitizer metadata, and object extensions, with any remainder up to the stride treated as poisoned padding. The stride size subtracts the left guard when guards are enabled, and the free link is stored at a cache specific offset inside the object.

Debug object validation aggregates independent checks into an overall pass flag. With guards it verifies left and right guards and an allocator size guard for active objects; without guards it verifies alignment filler under poisoning. Under poisoning it verifies free body and final byte patterns while skipping sanitizer owned prefix bytes for inactive objects, plus trailer padding. It then conditionally validates the free link and on failure reports corruption, clears the link, and marks failure.

Free link retrieval resets the tag, reads the stored value at the cache offset, and decodes it, with an optional hardened transform mixing cache randomness and the swapped link address. A null link is valid; otherwise the restored base must lie inside the slab range and align to the stride. Overlap between object body and link suppresses validation while the object is active.

Object error handling short circuits for test error injection, otherwise reports a slab bug, dumps slab information with the fault address for invalid pointers and a full object trailer for valid pointers, taints for bad paging with unreliable lock tracking, and warns.

Object trailer diagnostics print tracking records and slab information, then the object address with its offset from the slab base and its decoded free link. They show the left guard or preceding bytes, a bounded object window, the right guard when enabled, and a padding section only when the computed trailer end differs from the stride derived size.

Allocation tracking is inactive without the store user flag. When active it prints allocation and free records with call site, age derived from current time minus event time, processor, and process identifier, skipping empty records, and optionally prints a saved stack handle or notes a missing trace.

Pattern verification enables metadata access around an inverted memory scan after tag reset and succeeds when no mismatch exists. On mismatch it trims trailing expected bytes to isolate the corrupted span, suppresses prints for test injection, otherwise reports the affected range with offset and expected versus observed values plus an optional object dump, restores expected bytes over the span, and reports failure.

Padding verification computes the trailer end as information end plus optional user tracks and size word, sanitizer metadata, and object extensions, succeeds immediately when the end equals the stride derived size, and otherwise expects the live poison pattern over the remainder. A disabled debug configuration provides an empty pad check and an object check that always succeeds.

Slab teardown derives the backing page, block order, and page count, clears persistent allocation state and mapping, clears the slab marker, accounts reclaimed pages, performs cache specific unaccounting with a spin allowance, then releases the pages through the locked or lockless frozen path according to that allowance.

Cache option flags select debug behavior: a guard flag enables left and right guard handling and size adjustment, a poison flag enables fill verification and padding checks, an object poison subflag gates free body verification, a store user flag enables tracking records and trailer growth, and an allocator size flag enables original size handling.

Expected fill markers distinguish object states: one value marks active objects for guard checks, one marks live padding and alignment filler, one marks free body bytes, and one marks the final byte of a free object.

Frozen free control flags select preparation skipping and locking behavior, with distinct values for default handling, lockless handling, and already prepared pages. Migration selectors distinguish isolated blocks for direct return, a threshold for cacheable classes, and a movable fallback for high atomic and contiguous blocks.

Page validation masks select which flag bits are checked at preparation versus at free time, with separate masks for second page state and tail preparation clearing. A tail marker value identifies tail pages, and track selectors distinguish allocation from free records.
